Reduce the bend angle to keep the form coherent across views and avoid over-tiering.

rationale: The candidate reads as a single compact object and remains coherent in all four views, so the basic repair integrity is acceptable. However, it is still fundamentally a boxy, stepped/cantilevered extrusion with weak form continuity and only a minor void cue; the public edge is not strongly opened toward the access/frontage condition, so the required active ground threshold is underdeveloped. The visible silhouette is not an effective section program statement for neighborhood living: it suggests stacked massing more than a legible inhabited ground/public sequence. The references support either a more deliberate stepped/tapered upper profile or a clearer street-building threshold, but the candidate currently sits between those languages without fully committing to either. Because the program is neighborhood living and the ground/void relation is semantically central, the current mass does not hard-pass program fit.
